newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares closed almost unchanged on Tuesday, paring near all initial gains after profit-taking sapped market strength in the early afternoon and then a weaker start on Wall Street undermined the rally further.

The AEX index of blue-chip stocks sprinted ahead around five points at the start of the day, with sentiment buoyed by Monday's 74-point rally on Wall Street and an overnight dollar surge. Investor mood there was cheered by the belief that any interest rate rise may not be as fierce as originally thought.
But the strength was short-lived. The AEX ended the day at 526.26 points, up 0.62 but well off its earlier high of 567.21.

A weaker Dow opening on Tuesday helped to take off more of the shine as markets also absorbed comments from the Federal Reserve's Janet Yellen the U.S. had entered an inflationary daner zone but the outlook was unclear.
"The market started off looking very good but we seem to lost a bit of steam," one dealer here said, adding the underlying tone remained generally positive.

One stock that remained under pressure all day was brewing giant Heineken, which closed with losses of 7.30 guilders at 362.90. Dealers said talk of slower earnings per share growth prompted profit-taking ahead of Friday's half-year results.
"There are a few jitters around. People are worried about the prospects for growth," one dealer said, adding the soaring share price in the past two years gave scope for profit-taking.

High technology firm ASM Lithography ended 2.30 higher at 61.10 after the company moved earlier in the day to dispel market fears over its falling share price. ASM re-iterated its expectation that earnings per share would meet analysts' estimates of six to seven guilders for the full year 1996.
Nedlloyd had another good day as Monday's news of the merger of its container unit with P&O prompted follow-through interest. After rising 6.00 yesterday, it ended 1.50 up at 47.00 guilders.

Elsewhere, the firm dollar continued to give support to the heavyweight international stocks and most finished with good gains. Unilever put on 2.50 guilders to 253.70 and Royal Dutch was up 2.40 at 259.50 guilders.

Technical analysts said the AEX index could face a period of sideways trading or a small correction after rising around 20 points in the past two days, which was described as overdone. But dealers said chart resistance above 565 points was unlikely to hold a sustained market move for long.
